strategic_assessment.headline: The funnel has 13 breaks and content hasn't started — more outreach volume right now is pouring water into a leaking bucket.
strategic_assessment.body:
The org is running at split-personality mode. Nell is drafting POSSIBLE conference emails, Nova has 56 podcast shows in her pipeline, Zara is surfacing high-priority signals daily — the outbound engine looks busy. But Leo found 13 breaks between first touchpoint and closed deal: sprint pages with no prices, Google indexing dead products at wrong prices, cold email links that land on a homepage chatbot instead of a product. You are actively driving traffic into a broken funnel. The single highest-leverage move this week is not more outreach — it is approving Leo's top 3 fixes so Arlo can ship them in one afternoon.

Content is the second gap that's making everything harder. Cleo's two-week plan is built, structured, and ready to execute — but zero pieces are live. The POSSIBLE conference is 18 days away and Nell's outreach is landing cold because there is no credibility trail behind it. Every LinkedIn post that goes up this week makes the next podcast pitch, the next conference DM, and the next warm email land materially harder. Content is not a nice-to-have — it is the conversion multiplier for everything else currently in flight. Running outreach before content is backwards, and it costs you on every touch.

The org itself ran at roughly 60% capacity in Phase 2 week 1. Four agents — Cleo, Maya, Marcus, Scout — did not fire at all. This is a cron activation problem, not a capability problem, and it is solvable in under an hour. The agents that did run (Zara, Leo, Nova, Priya, Felix) produced high-quality, pass-rated work. The infrastructure is working where it is switched on. The priority right now is flipping the switches that are still off — starting with content and funnel, because those are the two outputs that unblock everything else.
strategic_assessment.recommended_focus: This week: approve Leo's top 3 funnel fixes (15 min read, Arlo ships same afternoon), check the Bob Pittman Gmail draft and greenlight Nell's batch, then approve Cleo's content plan so the first LinkedIn post goes live Thursday. Those three decisions, all under 40 minutes total, unlock conversion, conference outreach, and the content flywheel in one move.

metrics.label: Revenue MTD
metrics.interpretation: Zero revenue on Day 9 is not a demand problem — it is a conversion problem. Leo's audit found 13 funnel breaks, and the top two live on your highest-traffic pages: Sprint pages with no prices send self-qualifying buyers to a competitor.

metrics.label: Funnel Fixes Shipped
metrics.interpretation: Leo identified all 13 breaks and ranked the top 3 fixes that Arlo can ship in one afternoon — they are waiting on a single 15-minute Krish review. Every day they sit unactioned is another day of active trust damage in Google search results.

metrics.label: Content Pieces Live
metrics.interpretation: Cleo's two-week plan is fully built and structurally approved, but zero pieces are live — the flywheel is designed but not spinning, and POSSIBLE Conference is 18 days away making every day without content a missed credibility rep.

metrics.label: POSSIBLE Guest Confirmations
metrics.interpretation: Bob Pittman's test draft is sitting in Gmail drafts right now — one 5-minute read either unlocks the full Tier 1 batch or gives Nell exactly what she needs to revise. The conference window closes April 27.

metrics.label: Agent Coverage
metrics.interpretation: Half the roster ran successfully in week 1; Cleo, Maya, Marcus, Scout, and the efficiency agent never fired — 50% capacity means the org is producing half its designed intelligence and execution output, not because agents fail, but because their crons were never activated.

external_signals.recommended_action: Use the consolidation framing as Krish's LinkedIn angle this week (feed to Cleo as a hot topic override) and incorporate into every Nova pitch deck and speaking abstract currently in flight.
